title: Perseverance
summary: These passages describe endurance as a response to hardship, grounded in hope and sustained through faithful action. Romans 5 links suffering with endurance, character, and hope; Hebrews urges its readers to hold firm and run with perseverance; James says tested faith can produce endurance. The texts encourage continued faithfulness, but they do not all define perseverance in the same way or settle later debates about whether a believer can fall away.
historical_context: The cited material includes Paul’s letter to the Romans, exhortations in Hebrews, and the opening of James. The summary stays with the situations and arguments presented in those writings; the object’s sources do not support a more detailed social or historical reconstruction.
ancient_near_east_context: Ancient background for Perseverance includes covenant life, temple worship, royal ideology, wisdom teaching, and early church confession; the entry ties that world to Romans 5:1-5, Hebrews 3:14, hupomone, and sanctification without letting comparison replace the biblical witness.
canonical_context: Romans connects endurance with hope through suffering; Hebrews addresses readers who need to hold fast and continue; James reframes trials as an occasion in which tested faith can mature. Together these passages portray endurance as both sustained trust and continued practice, while speaking to their readers in distinct ways.
literary_context: Romans 5 gives a chain of consequences from suffering to hope. Hebrews uses exhortation and the image of a race, directing attention to Jesus. James addresses trials directly and links endurance with maturity. Recognizing these different forms helps readers hear encouragement, warning, and practical counsel without turning them into one formula.
covenantal_significance: The passages connect endurance with confidence in God and a life shaped by faith. Romans emphasizes hope, Hebrews calls for steadfastness, and James describes tested faith becoming mature. They encourage faithful persistence, but their short excerpts do not resolve every doctrinal question about perseverance.
canonical_role: This entry gathers New Testament teaching about enduring hardship in faith. Its references illuminate hope, steadfastness, and tested faith through different arguments rather than one single definition.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Perseverance in its immediate context before generalizing.
Do not flatten distinct passages into one slogan; let the canon keep its own shape.
